title: Concentration
html:
Concentration is a game mechanic used in spellcasting. Spells with the  Concentration tag require the caster to continuously focus on them in order to maintain their effects.

Caster needs to focus on maintaining this spell. They can only cast one concentration spell at a time, and their concentration might be broken when they take damage.

Overview

Most spells with a duration require the caster to concentrate to maintain the spell's effects for the full duration. These spells have the  Concentration in their description. If concentration on a spell is broken, the spell's effects end immediately.

A caster can only concentrate on a single spell at a time, which is automatic and immediate – casters automatically begin concentrating on spells which require it.

Ending concentration

Uninterrupted, concentration lasts for the spell's full duration.[1] Otherwise, concentration can be broken under the following circumstances:

Manually

Concentration can be manually interrupted at any time via the x on the concentrated spell's icon, next to the caster's main portrait. For Xbox/PlayStation, navigate to the action wheel and hold Y/Triangle, respectively.

Casting another concentration spell

If a caster tries to cast a spell which requires concentration while already concentrating on another, concentration on the first spell is broken, and its effects end immediately. The new spell is successfully cast only after concentration breaks on the previous spell. This can have material in-game consequences; for example, if the first spell was  Haste and its caster was its target, then an attempt to cast another concentration spell first breaks concentration on haste, giving the caster the  Lethargic, which then prevents the second spell from being cast.

Taking damage

When a caster is concentrating on a spell and takes damage, they attempt a Constitution save against a DC equal to half the damage taken, or 10, whichever is higher. If the save fails, concentration ends.[2] If the damage taken is reduced to zero (for example, due to certain equipment or feats), a concentration saving throw is not triggered. Note also that a roll of 1 on a concentration saving throw is a critical failure and almost always breaks concentration,[3] regardless of whether the bonus would have exceeded the DC.[4] Conversely, a roll of 20 on a concentration saving throw is a critical success.[5]

Leaving the party

Companions lose concentration when dismissed from the party.

Flee combat

Concentration is broken automatically after a character flees from combat using the "Flee Combat" in-game button; if a character flees from combat by moving away from enemies until it automatically exits turn-based mode, concentration is not broken.

Conditions

Some conditions also break concentration, without allowing a save:

  • Anything in SG_Incapacitated
  •  Downed
  •  Banished
  •  Sleeping
  •  Incapacitated
  •  Prone
  •  Rage
